authority_boundary: Coding tactic records are candidate or reviewed guidance for AI agents. They do not override repo-local source truth, local style, tests, security policy, or human gates.
confidence_methodology: Confidence is a categorical review label based on source evidence and local applicability notes, not a calculated score or probability.
promotion_policy: A tactic can be promoted only after observable use evidence, review of applicability/non-applicability, validation commands, and human approval when it changes future-agent defaults.

tactics.name: Python public API boundary
applies_when: A module or package exposes reusable functions, classes, or CLI-adjacent helpers.
does_not_apply_when: A one-off script has no stable import surface or downstream callers.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Premature public surfaces can freeze internal helpers and create compatibility burden.
agent_failure_modes_it_prevents: Blurring source authority between public and private helpers
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: AI-generated Python often grows files organically and may not mark a deliberate public boundary unless prompted.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Define the intended public API with public names or __all__; keep helpers private unless a caller needs them.
tactics.reuse_notes: Use to turn scripts into packages or stable templates; avoid for tiny disposable scripts.

tactics.name: Python dataclass value object
applies_when: Structured records need stable fields, immutability, and readable construction.
does_not_apply_when: The object requires identity mutation, polymorphic behavior, or runtime validation beyond simple types.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: A dataclass can hide needed validation or become a weak substitute for a domain model.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often keep JSON-like dictionaries throughout the implementation instead of converting at the boundary.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True) for simple value/config/result objects when validation is local and explicit.
tactics.reuse_notes: Good default for DAD registry and packet records when Pydantic is not needed.

tactics.name: Python NewType IDs
applies_when: IDs and refs share string representation but should not be mixed.
does_not_apply_when: The repo does not run static typing and the extra annotations would not be checked.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: NewType can create annotation clutter without runtime protection.
agent_failure_modes_it_prevents: Passing repo IDs where asset IDs are expected
Mixing policy IDs and route IDs
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Plain strings are easy to generate and appear to work until a boundary is crossed.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use typing.NewType for semantically distinct string IDs when static checks will run.
tactics.reuse_notes: Pair with mypy or pyright before relying on it for safety.

tactics.name: Python Protocol side-effect port
applies_when: Filesystem, database, clock, randomness, mail, or API access needs a testable boundary.
does_not_apply_when: The side effect is isolated and already covered by a simple function seam or fixture.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Too many protocols can make small code feel enterprise-heavy.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often write direct calls first and only abstract after tests become painful.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Define a typing.Protocol for external side effects when it makes tests faster and boundaries clearer.
tactics.reuse_notes: Use for meaningful boundary isolation, not for every helper function.

tactics.name: Python TypedDict JSON boundary
applies_when: Raw JSON/config/API dictionaries need a documented shape before conversion.
does_not_apply_when: Runtime validation is required and a schema or Pydantic model is already the boundary.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: TypedDict is not runtime validation and can give false confidence without tests or validators.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often treat JSON objects as ad hoc dictionaries unless instructed to mark the boundary.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use TypedDict for raw JSON/config dicts at the boundary, then convert to domain objects.
tactics.reuse_notes: Pair with jsonschema or parser tests for real runtime guarantees.

tactics.name: Python Enum/Literal closed state
applies_when: Statuses, decisions, risk levels, lanes, or modes form a closed vocabulary.
does_not_apply_when: The vocabulary is user-extensible or comes from external data without validation.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Overly closed states can reject legitimate external values or force noisy migrations.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Magic strings are shorter and often accepted by tests until edge cases appear.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use Enum, StrEnum, or Literal for closed vocabularies and centralize accepted values.
tactics.reuse_notes: Good for DAD schemas and command decisions when vocabularies are intentionally closed.

tactics.name: Python match closed variants
applies_when: Branching is over structured closed variants and pattern matching improves clarity.
does_not_apply_when: A simple if/elif is clearer or the variants are not structurally distinct.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Pattern matching can become clever boilerplate for ordinary conditionals.
agent_failure_modes_it_prevents: Deep nested if/elif over structured variants
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Many examples in training data predate Python match or avoid it for compatibility.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use match only when variants are closed and the structural patterns make the dispatch easier to audit.
tactics.reuse_notes: Check repo Python version before using.

tactics.name: Python ExitStack dynamic cleanup
applies_when: Code opens a dynamic number of resources or needs staged cleanup callbacks.
does_not_apply_when: A single ordinary with statement is sufficient.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: ExitStack can hide simple resource lifetime if used where nested with statements are clearer.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often open resources in loops and forget cleanup paths.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use contextlib.ExitStack for dynamic resource cleanup and staged callbacks.
tactics.reuse_notes: Especially useful for long-script refactors with many open files.

tactics.name: Python importlib.resources for package assets
applies_when: Code reads package-owned templates, schemas, prompts, or data files.
does_not_apply_when: The file is user-provided, repo-root-relative, or outside the package.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Confusing package resources with user files can make configuration hard to override.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Many examples use Path(__file__) because it works in source checkouts.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use importlib.resources for package-owned resources instead of brittle __file__ paths.
tactics.reuse_notes: Use when DAD scripts become installed package commands with bundled templates.

tactics.name: Python secrets, not random
applies_when: Code generates tokens, password reset URLs, API keys, nonces, or authentication randomness.
does_not_apply_when: Randomness is for simulation, sampling, tests, or non-security shuffle behavior.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Using secrets for deterministic tests can make failures hard to reproduce.
agent_failure_modes_it_prevents: False sense of security in AI-generated code
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Generic examples often import random first unless the prompt explicitly says security-sensitive.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use the secrets module for authentication or credential randomness; do not use random.
tactics.reuse_notes: Escalate to security review for token/session work.

tactics.name: Python contextvars request context
applies_when: Async or threaded code needs request/session context without global mutable state.
does_not_apply_when: The code is synchronous and explicit parameter passing is clearer.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Implicit context can hide dependencies and complicate tests.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may reach for module globals before considering async-local context.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use contextvars for async request/session context when explicit parameter passing would be too invasive.
tactics.reuse_notes: Prefer explicit parameters until async context pain is real.

tactics.name: Python singledispatch conversion boundary
applies_when: Type-based conversion/adaptation is growing into repeated if/elif chains.
does_not_apply_when: Only two simple cases exist or the dispatch key is not actually type-based.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: singledispatch can scatter conversions and make call paths harder to follow.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents tend to extend visible if/elif code rather than introduce dispatch boundaries.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use functools.singledispatch when type-based conversion is the clean boundary.
tactics.reuse_notes: Keep registrations near the domain boundary and test each supported type.

tactics.name: Python raise from causal errors
applies_when: Wrapping lower-level exceptions into domain-specific errors.
does_not_apply_when: The original exception should propagate directly or sensitive details must be suppressed carefully.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Over-wrapping can add noise or leak underlying sensitive error details.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often catch Exception and raise a new message without preserving the cause.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: When wrapping errors, use raise DomainError(...) from exc unless redaction requires suppression.
tactics.reuse_notes: In secret-handling code, ensure causal traces do not expose credentials.

tactics.name: Python characterization before refactor
applies_when: Refactoring long scripts or legacy behavior where intended outputs are not fully documented.
does_not_apply_when: The behavior is intentionally changing and new acceptance tests already define the target.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Characterization tests can freeze buggy behavior unless known-bug cases are labeled.
agent_failure_modes_it_prevents: False confidence from only testing new helpers
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often refactor first and add tests after the shape changes.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Before refactoring, add characterization tests for current behavior and label known bugs separately.
tactics.reuse_notes: Default for long-script refactors unless the user explicitly asks for behavior change.

tactics.name: Python functional core, imperative shell
applies_when: Parsing, validation, routing, or scoring can be pure while I/O remains at the edge.
does_not_apply_when: The workflow is inherently side-effectful and extracting a pure core would add confusion.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Over-extraction can fragment a simple script into too many tiny helpers.
agent_failure_modes_it_prevents: I/O mixed into parsing and validation
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often write an end-to-end script in execution order instead of separating pure logic.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Keep parsing/validation/calculation pure; put filesystem, network, and CLI output at the shell.
tactics.reuse_notes: Use when tests are slow because pure logic is trapped behind I/O.

tactics.name: Rust private by default
applies_when: Designing modules, crates, or libraries where public API should be deliberate.
does_not_apply_when: A binary-only prototype has no library boundary yet.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Overly private internals can make legitimate integration tests awkward.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may mark items pub to satisfy compiler errors quickly.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Keep Rust items private unless they are intended API; use pub(crate), pub(super), or pub(in path) deliberately.
tactics.reuse_notes: Default for Rust library design; relax only when API needs are real.

tactics.name: Rust public facade with pub use
applies_when: A crate wants a stable public API while hiding internal module layout.
does_not_apply_when: The module layout itself is intentionally public API.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Facade exports can obscure where items live if docs are weak.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often expose modules directly to make examples compile.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Re-export intended public API from lib.rs and keep internal module layout private.
tactics.reuse_notes: Best for libraries, not always necessary for binaries.

tactics.name: Rust newtype domain IDs
applies_when: IDs, refs, units, money, hashes, paths, or tokens share primitive representations but have domain meaning.
does_not_apply_when: A primitive is truly generic and carries no domain constraints.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Too many thin wrappers can slow development if conversions dominate the code.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: The compiler accepts String and u64 quickly, so the better boundary is easy to skip.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use newtypes for domain IDs and validate construction at the boundary.
tactics.reuse_notes: Strong fit for Rust shadow-layer identifiers and test parity maps.

tactics.name: Rust enums, not magic strings
applies_when: State machines, modes, decisions, or message types are closed sets.
does_not_apply_when: Values are externally extensible or schema-defined strings must remain open.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Closed enums can make extensions semver-sensitive.
agent_failure_modes_it_prevents: Unreachable states not checked by compiler
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: String comparisons are quick to write and easy to patch.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Model closed modes and states with enums and match exhaustively.
tactics.reuse_notes: Useful for Rust parity status and release gate decisions.

tactics.name: Rust Result error types
applies_when: A library or CLI needs meaningful recoverable errors and audit-friendly failure modes.
does_not_apply_when: A prototype or test can reasonably panic and the panic is localized.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Overly complex error enums can hide simple failure handling.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may use unwrap or anyhow-style strings to move quickly.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Return Result<T, E> with meaningful error types at library boundaries.
tactics.reuse_notes: Avoid broad anyhow at stable library API boundaries unless local policy allows it.

tactics.name: Rust private struct fields
applies_when: Struct invariants should be protected through constructors/accessors.
does_not_apply_when: A plain data transfer struct intentionally exposes all fields.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Too many accessors can make simple data awkward.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Public fields are convenient for tests and examples.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Keep struct fields private when invariants matter; expose constructors/accessors deliberately.
tactics.reuse_notes: Pair with builders when construction has many options.

tactics.name: Rust builder for complex values
applies_when: Construction has many optional fields, constraints, or staged validation.
does_not_apply_when: A simple constructor with a few required fields is clearer.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Builder boilerplate can obscure small value objects.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often pile parameters into one constructor until readability suffers.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use a builder when construction has many optional or constrained fields.
tactics.reuse_notes: Consider derive_builder or typed builders only after dependency review.

tactics.name: Rust sealed trait future-proofing
applies_when: A public trait should not be implemented by downstream crates because future evolution needs flexibility.
does_not_apply_when: Downstream implementations are the point of the trait.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Sealing a trait can block legitimate extension and frustrate library users.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: The pattern is specialized and not obvious from ordinary trait examples.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use the sealed trait pattern only when downstream implementations would break future evolution.
tactics.reuse_notes: Treat as library API design tactic requiring human review.

tactics.name: Rust trait ports for side effects
applies_when: Filesystem, network, database, clock, or service calls need testable boundaries.
does_not_apply_when: A direct call is simpler and already isolated behind one small function.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Unneeded traits can make ownership and generics harder to follow.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may push side effects into business logic and rely on integration tests later.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use traits as side-effect ports when they simplify tests or isolate external systems.
tactics.reuse_notes: Keep trait surfaces narrow and owned by the domain that consumes them.

tactics.name: Rust clippy and doc tests
applies_when: Rust code changes affect public APIs, examples, or library behavior.
does_not_apply_when: The repo has no Rust toolchain available and the task is documentation-only.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Running broad Rust checks blindly can be too slow without change scope or feature awareness.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may run cargo test only and miss clippy or docs.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: For Rust changes, run cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test, and cargo test --doc where appropriate.
tactics.reuse_notes: For large repos, route through change-aware orchestration instead of always running every feature matrix.

tactics.name: Short root instructions linked to profiles
applies_when: A persistent repo needs AI guidance that remains readable and maintainable.
does_not_apply_when: A one-off scratch repo has no durable AI navigation.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Too much indirection can hide critical local rules from the agent.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may paste comprehensive guidance into root files instead of linking task profiles.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Keep root agent instructions short; link to DAD profiles and local task-specific docs.
tactics.reuse_notes: Use managed pointers, not full asset copies, for downstream repos.

tactics.name: Goal, context, constraints, done-when
applies_when: A user or repo template defines repeatable agent task prompts.
does_not_apply_when: The request is a trivial command where added structure would slow the user down.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Rigid forms can become ceremony if they are required for tiny tasks.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Natural language requests often omit stop conditions unless the agent asks.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: For non-trivial work, define goal, context, constraints, and done-when criteria before implementation.
tactics.reuse_notes: Default for DAD mail implementation packets and repo-template prompts.

tactics.name: Plan before multi-file change
applies_when: A task changes multiple files, schemas, architecture, governance, or public behavior.
does_not_apply_when: The edit is a narrow typo or isolated test expectation update.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Planning can become overlong and stale if not tied to validation.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents can start editing quickly and discover dependencies late.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: State a short plan and validation path before multi-file or high-risk edits.
tactics.reuse_notes: Already aligned with DAD preflight/midflight rules.

tactics.name: Verifiable goals
applies_when: A task can be checked with tests, typechecks, linters, builds, screenshots, or exact behavioral checks.
does_not_apply_when: The work is exploratory research and no deterministic claim is made.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: A weak check can be treated as proof of broader correctness.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may report completion from local reasoning unless instructions require evidence.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Name the exact checks that will prove the change and report any checks not run.
tactics.reuse_notes: Make checks specific to task scope; avoid running huge batteries by default.

tactics.name: Midflight when stuck
applies_when: An agent is stuck, writing generic code, or facing an unfamiliar language/risk boundary.
does_not_apply_when: The next step is obvious and already covered by local authority.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Too many midflight checks can interrupt flow without improving correctness.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often continue with the first viable pattern rather than pause for better context.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: If the implementation starts feeling generic, ask DAD for tactic recommendations before writing more code.
tactics.reuse_notes: Useful when paired with concise output and explicit non-applicability notes.

tactics.name: Postflight pay-forward
applies_when: Material work revealed a useful tactic, failure, missing asset, or validation lesson.
does_not_apply_when: No material work occurred or no reusable observation exists.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Low-signal lessons can clutter preflight if promoted without review.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents often finish after tests and skip durable learning capture.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: After work, record which tactics helped, failed, or should be avoided, with evidence and context limits.
tactics.reuse_notes: Postflight feedback must separate confirmed findings, inferred findings, assumptions, and unknowns.

tactics.name: Agent instruction smell check
applies_when: A repo has bloated, stale, conflicting, or vague agent instructions.
does_not_apply_when: Instruction files are short, current, local-authority aligned, and validated.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Over-editing instruction files can accidentally change repo governance.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Agents may obey instructions without auditing whether the instructions are healthy.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Before adding new root instructions, check for instruction smells and prefer linked profiles or managed blocks.
tactics.reuse_notes: Use read-only review first; managed-block edits require target repo authorization.

tactics.name: Sandbox and permission minimum
applies_when: An agent works in unknown repos, runs commands, installs packages, uses MCP/plugins, or handles public/private boundaries.
does_not_apply_when: The task is read-only and uses no external tools or command execution.
tactics.danger_if_misapplied: Over-restricting permissions can block legitimate validation, but over-broad permissions can leak data or run untrusted code.
tactics.why_ai_may_underuse_it: Helpful agents may follow repo instructions or setup scripts without enough provenance skepticism.
tactics.example_prompt_instruction: Use least privilege, provenance checks, and human gates before running unknown code or moving private-origin material toward public repos.
tactics.reuse_notes: Default for public-safe mail provenance and unknown repo setup.
